root_topic: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body

branches.theme: 3.1 Culinary Heritage and Traditional Eating Maxims

details: Traditional food systems focus on seasonal, local, and balanced meals.
'Annena jatani jivanti': Food sustains life in all living creatures.
'Hitabhuk, Ritabhuk, Mitabhuk': Eat wholesome food, eat seasonal food, eat in measured moderation.
experiments_or_examples: Traditional Food Festival showcase with Dr. Poshita, Medu, and Mishti

details: Carbohydrates: Primary source of quick energy (rice, wheat, maize, sweet potato).
Fats: High-density energy storage and thermal insulation (ghee, oil, butter, nuts).
Proteins: Essential for body growth, cell building, and muscle repair (pulses, milk, paneer, roasted chana).
experiments_or_examples: Testing energy levels after consuming balanced meals vs fast food

details: Vitamins & Minerals: Protect against deficiency diseases and regulate body metabolism (fresh fruits, leafy greens, milk).
Dietary Fiber (Roughage): Indigestible plant material adding bulk to stool and aiding intestinal motility.
Water: Solvent for metabolic reaction transport and temperature regulation.
experiments_or_examples: Examining nutritional labels for fiber and mineral content

sub_branches.concept: Nutritional and Ecological Value of Millets
details: Millets are small-seeded, highly climate-resilient, drought-resistant cereal crops.
Rich in proteins, dietary fiber, iron, calcium, and micro-nutrients.
Major native Indian millets: Jowar (Sorghum), Bajra (Pearl Millet), Ragi (Finger Millet), Sanwa (Barnyard Millet).
Junk food (e.g., potato wafers, carbonated drinks) provides empty calories, excessive sodium, and unhealthy saturated fats with zero fiber or vitamins.
Wholesome traditional snacks (e.g., roasted chana, sprouts) deliver rich proteins, complex carbs, and essential fiber.
experiments_or_examples: Comparative activity analyzing packaging labels of potato wafers vs. roasted chana packet
